Conditional on the step history, the invariant is N(0,V) with positive variance perpetuity V=B+A Vprime, giving finite pth absolute moment iff E|R|^p<1 by geometric L^{p/2} estimates and strict monotone contradiction. A finite fourth moment also obeys a strictly positive fourth-moment recurrence, forcing E[R⁴]<1; for E[R⁴]<1 the causal series converges in L⁴. Algebra gives 3Var(Q)/(1-E[R⁴]). Both witness laws were recomputed using exact fractions: EH=1, EH²=5/4, m2=1/4, v=4/3, but m4 is 1/16 and 1261/576, with finite fourth 92/15 only for the former. The check program passes 210 exact rational parameter tests, not used as a substitute for infinite proof. For the second law M(3)=1297/1776<1<M(4), M(0)=1, Mprime(0)<0 and Mdoubleprime>0 prove the unique positive cutoff kappa in (3,4), while the first law has all moments finite.

value.rationale: Long-time invariant-measure accuracy is the mathematical purpose of stationary stochastic theta solvers. The exact Gaussianity iff characterization singles out midpoint as preserving the Gaussian equilibrium for any independent positive finite-support random steps. The exact criterion for all positive real moment orders and the explicit two laws with precisely matching mean, second moment and stationary variance but an all-moments-finite law versus one with a unique cutoff between the third and fourth moments demonstrate a substantively important rare-error reliability boundary missed by mean-square analysis. The counterexample remains meaningful despite scalar and fixed-distribution restrictions; no downstream speedup claim is made.
